jobs.description:
Note: By applying to this position you will have an opportunity to share your preferred working location from the following: **Mountain View, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA**.

### **Minimum qualifications:**

* Master's degree in Finance, Economics, quantitative fields, or equivalent practical experience.
* 5 years of institutional finance experience in investigative, modeling-intensive roles (Quantitative Trading, Corporate Finance, or Alternative Asset Management)**.**
* Experience with frontier LLMs, coding agents, or AI evaluation pipelines, including structured prompts and tool-use traces.
* Experience identifying flaws in AI-generated financial models, backtests, or memos, and translating these errors into generalizable grading rules.

  

### **Preferred qualifications:**

* CFA, CPA, MBA, JD, Master of Financial Engineering (MFE), or an advanced quantitative degree in Finance, Computer Science, Math, or Economics.
* Background building benchmarks, rubrics, or SFT/RLHF pipelines at AI labs, fintechs, or quantitative teams.
* Domain-specific excellence in Python and SQL (Quant) or advanced, macro-free spreadsheet software and Python/SQL (Alternative Asset Management/Corporate Finance).
* Familiarity with market data feeds, SEC EDGAR, Capital IQ, FactSet, Bloomberg, ERP/EPM, and tax/audit platforms.

**About the job**
-----------------

DeepMind is building frontier financial reasoning and agentic capabilities across Gemini and our enterprise agent harnesses. Moving AI from a generalist research assistant to an agent that can autonomously complete financial workflows requiresmore than raw pre-training scale - it requires deep domain mechanics embedded directly into how models are post-trained, how agent harnesses and tools are architected, and how evaluations measure real-world finance.

As a Finance Subject Matter Experts (SME), you will work with models, evaluations, and post-training data in the following three Finance domains -

* Quantitative Trading
* Corporate Finance - specifically with experience across FP&A, Audit and Tax
* Alternative Asset Management

Unlike traditional advisory roles that stop at high-level feedback or static prompt writing, you will sit directly in the model development loop alongside Research Scientists, Post-Training Engineers, and Product Managers. You will prioritize differentiated financial workflows, design end-to-end financial benchmarks, construct atomic and deterministic grading rubrics, diagnose multi-step agent trajectories, repair near-miss model reasoning traces, design verifiable reward signals, and co-build domain-specific agent skills.

Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At Google DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
  
  
US: $207000 - $300000 (USD) + 20% bonus target + equity + benefits  
  
Learn more about benefits at Google.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Evaluate the AI's step-by-step process across calculations, ledger searches, and code to pinpoint quantitative or accounting errors.
* Create realistic financial tasks (e.g., valuations, backtests, audits) and write "gold-standard" examples to correct model near-misses.
* Build complex prompts featuring vague instructions, GAAP/non-GAAP differences, and conflicting estimates to test AI resilience.
* Create pass/fail checklists for deliverables and draft deceptive, polished-but-wrong answers to stress-test automated graders.
* Teach the AI to efficiently use core financial tools (SQL, etc) and categorize error patterns into reusable templates.

**Position**: Laboratory Technician

**Who We Are**

AQUA-Science is an ELAP-certified aquatic toxicity testing laboratory located in Davis, California, and an MLJ Environmental company. Established in 1985, we have completed well over 8,000 toxicity tests using freshwater, estuarine, and marine organisms for NPDES compliance, stormwater, agricultural discharge, groundwater, and industrial discharge monitoring. We are a small laboratory with a focus on quality, and we have built a reputation as dependable, unbiased, and thorough experts.

AQUA-Science is seeking a full-time Laboratory Technician. This position conducts aquatic toxicity tests with a variety of aquatic organisms, including fish, invertebrates, plants, and algae. Working under the direct supervision of a Scientist or the Laboratory Supervisor, the Laboratory Technician prepares test solutions, performs water chemistry analyses, measures organism health, and makes sure test data are accurate and complete.

**Schedule and Salary**

This is a full-time, on-site position at our Davis laboratory (40 hours per week). The schedule is Tuesday through Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The hourly wage is $22 - $28 per hour based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision and retirement benefits (401k and profit-sharing).

**Required Skills/Qualifications**:

* B.S. in environmental toxicology, biology, or a related field.
* Ability to work under the direct supervision of a Scientist or Laboratory Supervisor.
* Working knowledge of basic scientific methods.
* Highly motivated and organized, with the ability to work well under pressure.
* Ability to use analytical instruments, scales, calculators, and all other commonly used laboratory equipment.
* Ability to work independently as well as within a team.
* Ability to follow written and verbal instructions.

**Job Duties**:

As a Laboratory Technician, you will conduct aquatic toxicity tests with a variety of aquatic organisms, including fish, invertebrates, plants, and algae. You will make dilutions of test solutions and perform water chemistry analyses for pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, alkalinity, hardness, ammonia, and other parameters. You will calibrate the analytical instruments used for these analyses and measure aquatic organism health, including survival, reproduction, and growth.

Accurate data is central to our work. You will enter data according to laboratory protocol and check data for correctness and completeness. You will work both independently and as part of a small team. We are looking for a motivated, organized individual who works well under pressure and is ready to contribute to the continued success of our laboratory.

To apply please send a 1) resume, 2) a cover letter and 3) contact information for three references to Trisha Turner (tturner @ aqua-science.com; please reference where you heard about this position in the email. Applications missing any of the above may not be considered for this position.

Additional information regarding AQUA-Science can be found on our website at www.aqua-science.com.

jobs.title: Lab Technician
jobs.description:
**Organization**: Rise Research

**Location**: Santa Clara, CA (in-person at Biocurious Lab, Santa Clara)

**Commitment:** Part-time, 3 hours per session, 2-3 times a week

**About the Role**

Rise Research is building a hands-on lab experiment program for high school students, combining real, in-person lab work with online mentor-led research training. Students run structured experiments (starting with Biofuel from Biomass) at a partner BSL-1 teaching lab, supported by a student portal and remote mentors.

The Lab Technician supervises every session on site: setting up the lab, overseeing students at the bench, checking their work at each stage, and keeping accurate records.

**What You'll Do**

* Prepare the lab before each session: set up benches, equipment, reagents, and consumables according to the experiment's equipment checklist (e.g., balances, pH meters, incubator/shaker, hotplate/stirrer, autoclave, and basic glassware)
* Take attendance and confirm every student has completed their safety sign-off and is wearing proper PPE (lab coat, gloves, goggles) before they begin
* Deliver the BSL-1 safety and lab orientation at the start of each experiment weekend
* Directly supervise all hands-on work. Students never use the biosafety cabinet, autoclave, hotplate, or incubator/shaker without supervision
* Guide students through each stage of the protocol, review the notes and photos they submit through the portal, and approve (or ask them to redo) each stage before they move on
* Check that raw data is recorded before any calculations are made, and flag unusual readings, skipped timepoints, instrument drift, or possible contamination
* Add lab technician notes to each student's stage history in the portal, and raise or resolve discrepancies as they come up
* Manage biological waste according to protocol, including autoclaving before disposal, signing off the waste log, and disinfecting benches and equipment after each session
* Maintain lab records: equipment checkout, inventory, consumables, and maintenance logs, and report shortages or equipment faults to the Head of Labs
* Stay in touch with remote mentors, who can see student notes and message you about individual students
* Share feedback on protocols, timing, and equipment so the program keeps improving

**Who You Are**

* Master’s degree (or equivalent hands-on experience) in a life sciences discipline such as biology, biotechnology, microbiology, biochemistry, or a closely related field
* Hands-on experience working in a BSL-1 laboratory, with solid knowledge of biosafety practices, aseptic technique, PPE, and biological waste handling
* Comfortable using common lab equipment such as pipettes, analytical balances, pH meters, incubators/shakers, autoclaves, and basic microscopes
* Patient, clear communicator who can explain technique to students who may be new to lab work
* Organized and detail-oriented, with accurate record-keeping
* Comfortable using a web-based portal to log notes, approvals, and records
* Prior experience teaching, tutoring, or mentoring students is a plus

**What We Offer**

* A part-time role
* The chance to be part of the founding team of a new student lab program
* Clear protocols, a purpose-built portal, and remote mentors to support you
* A collaborative, mission-driven team focused on giving students real research experience

If any questions, reach out to careers@riseglobaleducation.com

Pay: $50.00 - $80.00 per hour

Expected hours: 6.0 – 12.0 per week

**Postdoctoral Scholar**

Epstein Family Alzheimer’s Therapeutic Research Institute (ATRI), University of Southern California

**About Epstein Family ATRI**

The Epstein Family Alzheimer’s Therapeutic Research Institute (ATRI) at the University of Southern California serves as a coordinating center for multicenter clinical trials and longitudinal cohort studies in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias. ATRI supports trial design, data management, screening infrastructure, biomarker evaluation, and participant engagement across national and international research programs.

**Recruitment, Engagement, and Retention (RER) Section**

Within ATRI, the Recruitment, Engagement, and Retention (RER) Section conducts research using recruitment, screening, biomarker, cognitive, and longitudinal data generated through Alzheimer’s disease prevention trials and cohorts. The Section examines population heterogeneity across screening and participation pathways, biomarker-based eligibility, cognitive outcomes, and participant engagement and retention, with the goal of generating evidence that can inform future prevention research.

**Location: San Diego, CA**

**Position Summary**

Epstein Family ATRI is seeking a Postdoctoral Scholar to join the RER Section and contribute to an evolving program of Alzheimer’s disease prevention and clinical-trial research. The scholar will work with trial-embedded and longitudinal datasets that include recruitment and screening information, blood-based biomarkers, amyloid PET, cognitive measures, participant characteristics, and longitudinal outcomes. Scientific questions may examine who is identified through different screening approaches, who meets biomarker-based eligibility criteria, who participates and remains in longitudinal research, and how cardiometabolic, vascular, social, and other factors relate to cognitive outcomes and participation. The scholar will have opportunities to develop scientific questions, lead abstracts and first-author manuscripts, and build an increasingly independent research trajectory while working closely with RER faculty, clinical-trial investigators, and statistical collaborators.

This is a 12-month appointment, renewable for up to 24 months total, contingent upon funding, focused on advancing defined manuscript outputs tied to ongoing funded studies. The role operates within established analytic governance structures and collaborates with faculty and statistical teams to advance peer-reviewed publications.

This position does not involve operational study management, recruitment oversight, or statistical leadership.

Prospective candidates should submit a CV detailing relevant professional, academic, and research experience.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and advance scientific questions using recruitment, screening, biomarker, cognitive, and longitudinal data from Alzheimer’s disease prevention trials and cohorts.
* Lead manuscript development from completed and maturing analyses, including first-author manuscripts and collaborative publications.
* Translate statistical outputs into rigorous scientific interpretation and narrative in collaboration with faculty and statistical teams.
* Integrate relevant literature to frame findings within Alzheimer’s disease prevention and clinical-trial research.
* Participate in multidisciplinary scientific discussions within established Section and statistical governance structures.
* Contribute to abstracts, scientific presentations, and peer-reviewed publications.

**Reporting Structure**

The Postdoctoral Scholar reports to Dr. Doris Molina-Henry, MPI of APEX, within the Recruitment, Engagement, and Retention (RER) Section, and collaborates with Section leadership, ATRI faculty and statistical teams under existing analytic governance.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* PhD in epidemiology, public health, neuroscience, population health, or related field.
* Demonstrated experience interpreting complex longitudinal or trial-embedded datasets in collaboration with statistical teams.
* Strong scientific writing skills, including first-author manuscript drafting.
* Experience integrating biomarker, cognitive, clinical, behavioral, or population-level data into scientific interpretation.
* Ability to structure and advance manuscripts from analytic outputs to submission.
* Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within multi-investigator research environments.
* Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within multi-investigator research environments

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working with screening cohorts or biomarker-based trial populations.
* Experience examining population heterogeneity, longitudinal trajectories, or subgroup patterns.
* Experience contributing to multi-author manuscripts within clinical research settings.
* Ability to synthesize findings across related datasets and scientific domains.

**Position**: Laboratory Technician

**Who We Are**

AQUA-Science is an ELAP-certified aquatic toxicity testing laboratory located in Davis, California, and an MLJ Environmental company. Established in 1985, we have completed well over 8,000 toxicity tests using freshwater, estuarine, and marine organisms for NPDES compliance, stormwater, agricultural discharge, groundwater, and industrial discharge monitoring. We are a small laboratory with a focus on quality, and we have built a reputation as dependable, unbiased, and thorough experts.

AQUA-Science is seeking a full-time Laboratory Technician. This position conducts aquatic toxicity tests with a variety of aquatic organisms, including fish, invertebrates, plants, and algae. Working under the direct supervision of a Scientist or the Laboratory Supervisor, the Laboratory Technician prepares test solutions, performs water chemistry analyses, measures organism health, and makes sure test data are accurate and complete.

**Schedule and Salary**

This is a full-time, on-site position at our Davis laboratory (40 hours per week). The schedule is Tuesday through Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The hourly wage is $22 - $28 per hour based on experience. Benefits include health, dental, vision and retirement benefits (401k and profit-sharing).

**Required Skills/Qualifications**:

* B.S. in environmental toxicology, biology, or a related field.
* Ability to work under the direct supervision of a Scientist or Laboratory Supervisor.
* Working knowledge of basic scientific methods.
* Highly motivated and organized, with the ability to work well under pressure.
* Ability to use analytical instruments, scales, calculators, and all other commonly used laboratory equipment.
* Ability to work independently as well as within a team.
* Ability to follow written and verbal instructions.

**Job Duties**:

As a Laboratory Technician, you will conduct aquatic toxicity tests with a variety of aquatic organisms, including fish, invertebrates, plants, and algae. You will make dilutions of test solutions and perform water chemistry analyses for pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, alkalinity, hardness, ammonia, and other parameters. You will calibrate the analytical instruments used for these analyses and measure aquatic organism health, including survival, reproduction, and growth.

Accurate data is central to our work. You will enter data according to laboratory protocol and check data for correctness and completeness. You will work both independently and as part of a small team. We are looking for a motivated, organized individual who works well under pressure and is ready to contribute to the continued success of our laboratory.
